vo.text: If you know a surah by heart, there is a good chance it comes from tonight's part of the Quran.
The Quran is divided into thirty parts. Each part is called a juzz.
Many families read one juzz every night of Ramadan, so that by the end of the month, they have read the whole Quran.
Tonight we reach the last one. Juzz thirty. People call it Juzz Amma, after its very first word.
It holds thirty seven surahs. Most of them are short, and that is why children often learn them first.
Tonight, we open three treasures inside it.
The first treasure is Surah al-Alaq.
Its first five verses were the very first words of the Quran ever sent down, in the cave of Heera.
Read, in the name of your Lord, who created.
So the last part of the Quran holds its very first words. The end, and the beginning, side by side.
The second treasure is Surah al-Qadr. It tells us about one special night.
Allah says: We sent it down on the Night of Decree.
And the Night of Decree is better than a thousand months.
A thousand months is more than eighty three years. More than a whole lifetime, in a single night.
That night is hidden in the last ten nights of Ramadan, most likely on an odd night. So people give their best on every one of them.
The third treasure is tiny. Only four verses. Surah al-Ikhlaas.
Say: He is Allah, the One. Allah, the One everyone turns to. He has no child, and He was not born. And there is nothing like Him.
The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said that this little surah is equal to one third of the Quran.
And the last two surahs of the Quran, al-Falaq and an-Naas, are prayers for protection.
Every night before he slept, the Prophet recited them, together with al-Ikhlaas.
So tonight, before you sleep, you can do the same.
Thirty nights. Thirty lanterns. Tonight, the sky is full.
Do not put the lamp out.
Tomorrow morning: Eid.
